title: Codify Sustainability-Linked Sovereign Lending, Then Give It Scale
subtitle: Standard indicators, verification and pricing, and a reward bigger than an interest margin
message: Sustainability-linked debt pays governments for climate results, but each deal is bespoke and small. Codify indicators, verification and pricing; give investors a fixed coupon; and make guarantee capacity, not a few basis points, the prize.

problem.title: It works, and it is far too small

stats.label: the most Uruguay's $350m World Bank loan (2023) can save: about $8m in present value
value of a 100 bp step-down on a $1bn loan over ten years
cost of a stylized reform retiring 2 GW of coal ten years early

problem.text: Even waiving all interest on $1 billion at 6 percent is worth only $463 million. A rebate cannot exceed the interest bill, so interest margins are an order of magnitude too small for major reforms.

mechanism.title: Make guarantee capacity the reward
mechanism.caption: Present value at 5% over ten years, US$ million, log scale. Hatched: cost to the funder on the MDB loss record.
points: Codify: outturn indicators, baselines set by rule, published data, a price per tonne.
Investors hold a fixed coupon; an intermediary refunds interest when targets are met.
$3.3bn of capacity is worth $772m, the reform's cost; the funder expects to lose about $10m on the MDB record, $286m in the stress case.

action.title: The rebate is the signal; the guarantee pays
results: About 80 dollars of incentive per dollar of funder cost on the MDB loss record; 2.7 in a stress case without preferred-creditor status, with a $310m buffer held, not spent.
The government's exposure becomes smaller, contingent and contracted, not zero.
One verification can drive both the rebate and the guarantee capacity.
todo: MDBs: publish an indicator menu, baselines and a pricing schedule.
Back a fixed-coupon intermediary; missed targets fund corrective help, not bondholders.
Donors: make guarantee capacity the main prize and fund its buffer.
